I farm 20 mu, so I do not treat every mu the same, but I still look at the whole year together. I have done this for 30 years, and I do not like making big changes unless I can see the benefit clearly. On wheat and maize, I will mostly follow the way that has worked here in Quzhou County, then adjust a little for cost and yield. Wheat and maize are my main grain crops, so I would rather spend a bit more on fertilizer than let the field go hungry. I have well irrigation, so I can push yield more steadily than depending only on rain. For wheat, I will use improved seed, enough base fertilizer, and I will water around key times like overwintering, jointing, and grain filling if the weather needs it. For summer maize, I will use hybrid seed because the yield is more reliable, and around here people do that already. I will feed maize a bit heavier on nitrogen because it responds fast, and I will keep the field clean and spray when pests come. Chrysanthemum is different from grain. It needs cleaner management and more careful pest control, and the price can be better, so I will keep a smaller area on it and manage it more carefully with more potassium and more sprays. Some family members work off-farm, so I also think about labor. I will keep the grain area large and stable, and keep chrysanthemum to a size I can still manage well.
